literal: If one, disregarding the measure of their digestive fire, without discerning, eats excessively, disease will arise without limit.
translation: If a person eats excessively without discerning and disregarding the measure of their digestive fire, diseases will arise without limit.
modern: தன் பசித் தீயின் அளவை ஆராய்ந்து அறியாமல், ஒருவன் மிகுதியாக உண்டால், அவனுக்கு நோய்கள் எல்லையின்றி உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of eating according to one's digestive capacity, referred to metaphorically as 'tī' (fire). The word 'teriyāṉ' refers to a person who does not analyze or understand this capacity. When such a person eats excessively ('perituṇṇiṉ'), ignoring the limits of their digestive fire, it leads to severe consequences. The result is that diseases ('nōy') will arise in them without any limit ('aḷaviṉṟi'). Thus, moderation based on personal digestive strength is key to preventing endless illnesses.
